

WL-REQ-1317 v3: a selection on a spec is a byte range of that document
version's rendered body, and the server maps it onto the arranged rule's
text or the spec's template text it came from. `internal/store/docrender.go`
already concatenates the two (`renderBody` over `arrangedTexts`;
`bumpDocVersion` in `versions.go` uses the same pair for the snapshot).

- Add `renderSpans(body string, texts []arrangedText) (rendered string,
  spans []renderedSpan)` beside `renderBody`, where a `renderedSpan` is
  `{Start, End int; Rule int64; RuleVersion int; Offset int}`: the rendered
  byte range of one arranged rule's body with the offset of its first byte
  in `rule_versions.body`, or of one stretch of template text with the
  offset into `docs.body`; derived heading lines (`## 4. Title (WL-REQ-n)
  {#sec-4}`) are their own spans belonging to neither. `renderBody` must
  equal `rendered`, held by a test over the corpus fixtures `docrender_test.go`
  already uses.
- `mapRenderedRange(tx, docID, version, start, end int) (model.ReviewAnchor,
  error)`: refuses `version != docs.version` (Decisions), renders the
  current arrangement, finds the span containing `start`, and requires `end`
  to fall in the same span; a rule span yields `{Rule, Version: RuleVersion,
  ByteStart: start - Start + Offset, ByteEnd: ...}`, a template span yields
  `{Doc, Version, ByteStart, ByteEnd}` into `docs.body`, a heading span or
  a range that leaves its span is `ErrInvalidInput` naming the two spans
  (section anchors). `Quote` is checked by `OpenThread` afterwards against
  the mapped text, so a quote taken from the rendered text still has to
  equal the stored bytes.
- `OpenThread` calls it whenever `in.Anchor.Doc` names a spec and the
  anchor has a range; a plan's range is already into `docs.body` and needs
  no mapping. The stored thread is a `rule_id` or `doc_id` thread exactly as
  WL-REQ-1317 says: bytes inside a rule belong to the rule.

First store test:

```go
func TestMapRenderedRange(t *testing.T) {
    // spec with template preamble P, rule R1 (body B1), template text T between, rule R2 (body B2).
    // rendered := renderBody(...); i := strings.Index(rendered, B1[4:12])
    // mapRenderedRange(doc, cur, i, i+8) → Anchor{Rule: R1.ID, Version: R1.v, ByteStart: 4, ByteEnd: 12}
    // a range inside T → Anchor{Doc: doc.ID, Version: cur, ByteStart/End into docs.body}; docs.body[s:e] == rendered[i:j]
    // a range from the end of B1 into T → ErrInvalidInput naming sec-1 and the template
    // a range over R1's heading line → ErrInvalidInput
    // version cur-1 → ErrInvalidInput
    // OpenThread with {Doc: spec, Version: cur, range into B1, Quote: B1[4:12]} → stored rule_id = R1.ID
}
```

- [ ] `go test -trimpath ./internal/store -run 'TestMapRenderedRange|TestRenderSpans|TestRenderBody' -count=1` against Postgres — `ok`.
- [ ] Commit: `store: a range on a rendered spec maps onto the rule or template bytes it came from (WL-REQ-1317)`.
